title: Grade 4 Science — Thu, May 28
description: Rocks & Minerals — Day 4 of 5: The Rock Cycle
subject: science

questions.question: What is the rock cycle?
options: The continuous process by which rocks change from one type to another over time
questions.explanation: The rock cycle shows how igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks continuously change into one another through natural processes.

questions.question: In the rock cycle, what happens to magma when it reaches Earth's surface?
options: It becomes lava and cools into igneous rock
questions.explanation: Magma that erupts becomes lava. When lava cools, it hardens into igneous rock (e.g., basalt).

questions.question: What breaks rocks into smaller pieces over time?
questions.explanation: Weathering (wind, rain, ice) breaks rocks apart. Erosion carries the pieces away as sediment.

questions.question: Sediment is transported by rivers and eventually settles at the bottom of seas. Over millions of years it becomes:
questions.explanation: Sediment layers get buried, compressed, and cemented → sedimentary rock. This takes millions of years.

questions.question: What two conditions change sedimentary rock into metamorphic rock?
questions.explanation: Deep inside Earth, high heat and immense pressure transform existing rocks into metamorphic rock without melting them.

questions.question: What happens to metamorphic rock if it gets even hotter?
options: It melts into magma, restarting the cycle
questions.explanation: Extreme heat melts metamorphic rock into magma. Magma can then erupt as lava and cool into igneous rock again — cycle continues!

questions.question: Igneous rock exposed at the surface is weathered. Its pieces settle as sediment. Eventually they become:
questions.explanation: Igneous → weathering → sediment → compaction → sedimentary rock. A classic rock cycle path.

questions.question: How long does the rock cycle take?
options: Always the same amount of time
questions.explanation: Rock cycle processes are very slow — sedimentary rock formation takes millions of years; even weathering takes thousands.

questions.question: Limestone (sedimentary) is buried deep underground. Heat and pressure act on it. It becomes:
questions.explanation: Limestone + heat + pressure = marble (metamorphic). This is a classic rock cycle transformation.

questions.question: Can an igneous rock become metamorphic directly?
options: No — must go through sedimentary first
Yes — if it is buried under enough heat and pressure
questions.explanation: Yes! Any rock type can become metamorphic if subjected to high heat and pressure. Igneous → metamorphic is a valid path.

questions.question: Why is the rock cycle called a 'cycle'?
options: It only goes in one direction
Rocks are recycled over and over — there is no start or end
questions.explanation: It is a cycle because rocks continuously transform from one type to another with no fixed beginning or end — always ongoing.

questions.question: Volcanic island forms. Rain weathers the rocks. Rivers carry sediment to the ocean. Layers build up. What rock forms?
questions.explanation: Sediment layers from the weathered volcanic rock accumulate on the ocean floor and eventually form sedimentary rock.

questions.question: In the rock cycle, where does new material come from?
options: From the mantle (magma) — Earth continuously generates new material
Material never changes — same rocks forever
questions.explanation: Earth's mantle provides magma — new igneous rock material. The rock cycle moves this material through different forms.

questions.question: A mountain range erodes completely over millions of years. Where does the rock go?
options: It becomes sediment, then sedimentary rock, then possibly re-enters the cycle
questions.explanation: Eroded material becomes sediment → carried by water → deposited → forms sedimentary rock → may be subducted → metamorphic or magma. Rock is recycled, not lost.

questions.question: Rock cycle summary: correct order for one possible path?
options: Magma → Igneous → Weathering → Sediment → Sedimentary → Heat+Pressure → Metamorphic → Melt → Magma
questions.explanation: One complete cycle path: Magma cools → Igneous → Weathered → Sediment → Sedimentary → Heat+Pressure → Metamorphic → Melts → Magma again.
